answer: Sparse reach quorum. Each agent's record must be endorsed by peers occupying distinct regions of the interaction graph, verified against a signed routing log rather than any credential. A quill marks each route a signature traverses, so clones confined to one neighborhood fail to gather the required spread. Honest agents sit in a connected meadow of routes; attackers must plant isolated agents and pay the routing latency to bridge them. The per-identity cost is genuine message traffic across the ridge separating sybil clusters.
